text:
ana: Just got a bug report: AsyncClient instantiation in a running loop crashes with RuntimeError. Minimal repro in a FastAPI app.

ana: User snippet:
```
from redwood import AsyncClient
c = AsyncClient()
await c.embed('hi')
```

ana: stack shows our __init__ calling asyncio.run() for token refresh.

irene: yeah we've been using asyncio.run as a shortcut when no loop was found. That's not safe in library code.

matt: we need a clear pattern: never call asyncio.run in __init__. Two safe approaches:
- if get_running_loop succeeds -> schedule background task with create_task
- otherwise -> spin up a dedicated thread with its own new_event_loop and use run_coroutine_threadsafe

sasha: want to propose API change instead of silent behavior: add AsyncClient.from_sync() which intentionally creates a background thread loop, and keep AsyncClient() pure-async (doesn't start threads). Then people using frameworks or notebooks will do the right thing.

ana: that sounds reasonable and reduces surprise. We should deprecate the old behavior and add a migration note.

irene: implementation notes: when using thread loop, call asyncio.new_event_loop() inside the thread, run loop.run_forever(), and schedule the refresh via asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe. Also create httpx.AsyncClient lazily on the same loop to avoid TLS/socket issues.

matt: good call about httpx: transports are bound to the loop where the connection was opened. If we create the transport on main thread but then use another loop TLS handshakes can stall. Lazy-creation or keeping client and transport lifecycle in the same loop/thread is crucial.

sasha: add tests:
- pytest-asyncio test: instantiate AsyncClient inside a running loop, await a no-op method, assert no error and refresh task exists.
- threaded integ test: call AsyncClient.from_sync() in a sync test, then use run_coroutine_threadsafe to call generate concurrently, assert responses.
- junit-style notebook smoke test: start a simple ipykernel, import AsyncClient, run embed call to ensure no deprecation warnings about event loop.

ana: also add a short README section "Using AsyncClient in frameworks and notebooks" with dos/don'ts. That will cut down support tickets.

irene: we should avoid touching loop policies or recommending uvloop installs inside SDK init. If users change loop policy it should be their responsibility. Mention uvloop caveats in docs.

ci-bot: Created issue #1532: "AsyncClient should not call asyncio.run in __init__; add explicit sync constructor and tests" https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/1532

sasha: I'll take the PR. Will include the tests and doc blurb. Marking P1 for DX.

ana: thanks! I'll attach the user's repro and confirm once PR lands.
